title: Screen flickering on startup with Forward+ renderer on Windows (NVIDIA RTX 5080)
body:
### Tested versions

4.6.1.stable

### System information

Godot v4.6.1.stable - Windows 11 - Vulkan (Forward+) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 Monitor: 3440x1440 @ 60Hz

### Issue description

### Issue Description
When launching a Godot project with the Forward+ renderer on Windows, the game screen flickers on startup. The flickering occurs within the game window only (not the entire monitor).

Key observations:

1. Flickering happens on game startup, before any scene is loaded
2. Resizing the window changes the flickering state:
   - No flicker → resize → flicker appears
   - Flicker → resize → flicker disappears
   - Maximizing window causes flicker
3. Window has trailing/ghosting artifacts
4. A new empty Godot project does NOT have this issue
5. The issue is project-specific but not related to scene content
Frame timing analysis:

- Average frame time: ~37-38ms (should be ~16.67ms for 60fps)
- Frame drops: 110-124 per 10 seconds
- Max frame time: 107-195ms

### Workarounds Attempted
Workaround Result VSync Enabled (1) Partial improvement VSync Mailbox (3) Partial improvement VSync Disabled → Enabled toggle (Issue #104369) Did not resolve Window resize via code Partial improvement Windows API DWM fixes via Python Partial improvement stretch_mode = viewport Partial improvement

### Related Issues
- #104369 - Monitor flickers on focus change if app starts with Vsync OFF
- #80542 - Screen flicker/black screen when using the editor
- #110471 - VSync Jitter with dual GPU in Windows 11
### Additional Context
The issue appears to be related to render/frame synchronization between Godot's Vulkan renderer and Windows DWM (Desktop Window Manager). The fact that resizing the window changes the flickering state suggests a synchronization timing issue.

### Steps to reproduce

Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a Godot 4.6.1 project with Forward+ renderer
2. Configure VSync mode (tested with Adaptive, Enabled, Mailbox)
3. Launch the game
4. Observe screen flickering
5. Resize window - flickering state changes
